searchText: That's my understanding and I think it's covered by `get_safe_execution_payload_hash`: https://github.com/ethereum/consensus-specs/blob/dev/fork_choice/safe-block.md#get_safe_execution_payload_hash Ah that's the bit of spec I was looking for. Couldn't find it in the execution-api specs. Regarding EL sync post-merge, it seems to me that EL's should be able to use a recent finalized block as a pivot for world state, but also as the root for a backward sync of the blockchain. Is there any reason an EL could not simply download the pivot block, prioritize syncing the world state, and be "up"? Then EL could import the rest of the blockchain backward from the initial pivot block. it seems like this would be the strategy to support sync post eip-4444 talking with <@680337202521440470> , for this to be a viable strategy all of our pivots blocks would have be finalized. (or at least the final pivot block would have to be finalized). Otherwise we could end up with a world state that is isolated on a fork, unable to reorg to the canonical chain. I believe that is the case in-general post-merge, not just if we want to backward sync the blockchain

Regarding EL sync post-merge, it seems to me that EL's should be able to use a recent finalized block as a pivot for world state, but also as the root for a backward sync of the blockchain.

Is there any reason an EL could not simply download the pivot block, prioritize syncing the world state, and be "up"?  Then EL could import the rest of the blockchain backward from the initial pivot block.
